title: Get jansson reference counts right
summary: Stop json_object_set from leaking values, using json_object_set_new and json_decref.

turns.user: valgrind shows a ton of definitely lost in build_user. am i using jansson wrong?

assistant.body: Great question! json_string and json_integer return a fresh value with a reference count of 1. json_object_set then adds a reference of its own, so the caller's reference is never given back. When a value is created only to be inserted, json_object_set_new is the one to use, because it takes over that reference. root itself also needs a json_decref at the end, or the whole tree leaks. Note: the string from json_dumps belongs to the caller, who frees it with free.

turns.user: add a tags array too. frontend wants the same tags under meta as well

assistant.body: Sure. One tags array, hung under both root and meta. Both inserts take a value that was just created, so both use set_new. In other words, the caller is left with no reference to release.

Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. set_new hands over one reference, and tags only had one, so it was handed over twice. When root is freed, the first json_decref on tags destroys it and the second touches freed memory. The second insert should be json_object_set, which adds a reference of its own. tags then sits at a count of 2 and json_decref(root) releases both.
